definitions.explanation: The third story of a multi-story building. Note that in Japan (as in most of Asia), the first floor ({一階|いっかい}) is the ground floor, so {三階|さんがい} corresponds to what would be the 'second floor' in British English.

examples.japanese: ⟦{事務所|じむしょ}→事務所：01032_jimusho⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三階|さんがい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: The office is on the third floor.

examples.japanese: ⟦エレベーター→エレベーター：01340_erebeetaa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{三階|さんがい}⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{上|あ}がって→上がる：00615_agaru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please take the elevator up to the third floor.

examples.japanese: ⟦デパート→デパート：01022_depaato⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{三階|さんがい}{婦人服売|ふじんふくう}り⟦{場|ば}→場：03699_ba⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦セール→セール：07780_seeru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{始|はじ}まった→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧。
examples.english: A sale has begun in the third-floor women's clothing section of the department store.

notes:
⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧ (three) + ⟦{階|かい}→階：01034_kai⟧ (floor, story). The reading of ⟦{階|かい}→階：01034_kai⟧ undergoes rendaku to がい after ⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧.

PRONUNCIATION:
Both さんがい and さん⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧い are heard, but さんがい is the traditional and more common reading. The non-rendaku さん⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧い is increasingly used by younger speakers, especially because the homophone ⟦{三回|さんかい}→三回：30448_sankai⟧ (three times) is read with the same さん⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧い — this can cause confusion in speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三階|さんがい}{建|だ}て: three-story (building)
- {三階|さんがい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{上|あ}がる→上がる：00615_agaru⟧: to go up to the third floor
- {三階|さんがい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧: third-floor window

COUNTING FLOORS:
- ⟦{一階|いっかい}→一階：27512_ikkai⟧: first floor (ground floor)
- ⟦{二階|にかい}→二階：27513_nikai⟧: second floor
- {三階|さんがい}: third floor
- {四階|よんかい}: fourth floor
- {五階|ごかい}: fifth floor
